# Results — Study 662 (EM-Local-Bonds)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**emerging-market LOCAL-currency bonds pay a fat yield that compensates you for the risk, a
better carry than USD-denominated EM debt** — tested as a total-return, excess-of-cash spread
between a Local basket (average of EBND and LEMB) and EMB (USD EM), over the sample where all
six instruments co-exist. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `3b8388526303` (combined EBND/LEMB/EMB/AGG/UUP/BIL
adjusted-close panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return-adjusted closes (`auto_adjust=True`) for EBND, LEMB, EMB, AGG, UUP, BIL; 5,724 rows 2003-09-29 → 2026-06-30 |
| Common sample | **2011-11-30 → 2026-06-30, 176 months** — the first full month after LEMB's 2011-10-20 inception, the latest of the six instruments to launch |
| Statistics | paired one-sample *t* on the monthly Local-minus-EMB spread; **Newey-West (HAC)** *t* at 3/6/12-month lags as the serial-correlation-robust primary; a **circular block-bootstrap** (5,000 draws, 6-month blocks) 95% CI on the annualized gap; Wilson interval on the hit rate |
| Execution / costs | buy-and-hold exposure comparison, **no signal to lag** (the house convention exempts calendar-known, non-discretionary holdings — same as a scheduled-calendar entry); one-way one-time entry cost (5/10 bps) shown explicitly, amortized over 14.7 years — negligible by construction, reported for transparency, not because it moves the verdict |
| Data quirks (named) | `LEMB` switched from monthly to annual distributions around 2018 (fund-structure change) — irrelevant here since total-return-adjusted closes already fold every distribution into the price series regardless of frequency |

No survivorship: EBND, LEMB, EMB, AGG, UUP and BIL are all single funds tracking broad indices
still open today, not a cross-sectional panel of picks.

## The headline — Local (avg EBND/LEMB) minus EMB (USD EM), excess-of-cash

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| mean monthly gap | **−24.6 bps/mo** (−2.96%/yr) |
| paired *t* (no HAC) | **−1.97** |
| Newey-West *t* (lags 3 / 6 / 12) | **−2.02 / −2.16 / −2.17** |
| circular block-bootstrap 95% CI (annualized) | **[−5.62%, −0.20%]** — wholly below zero |
| hit rate (Local beats EMB, month-to-month) | **73/176 = 41.5%** (Wilson 95% [34.5%, 48.9%]) |

The claimed benefit does not show up. Every Newey-West lag choice (3, 6, 12 months) clears the
**|t| ≥ 2** bar in the *negative* direction, and the block-bootstrap 95% CI on the annualized
gap sits entirely below zero — this is not "no different from EMB", it is a robustly-identified
**underperformance**. Local beat EMB in only 41.5% of months, a hit rate whose Wilson interval
excludes 50%.

## Sharpe race — excess of cash (BIL), full sample

| leg | Sharpe (excess of cash) |
|---|--:|
| **Local** (avg EBND/LEMB) | **−0.023** |
| **EMB** (USD EM) | **+0.296** |
| **AGG** (US aggregate) | **+0.138** |

Fourteen and a half years of holding local-currency EM debt delivered a Sharpe ratio
*indistinguishable from zero* above cash — worse than both the USD EM benchmark it was supposed
to beat and the plain US aggregate bond fund an investor could have owned instead.

## One-time entry cost (buy-and-hold — no periodic turnover to charge)

| cost (one-way, one-time) | gross gap | net gap |
|---|--:|--:|
| 5 bps | −2.96%/yr | −2.96%/yr |
| 10 bps | −2.96%/yr | −2.96%/yr |

A static exposure comparison has one entry, not a repeated turnover drag; amortized over 176
months the cost is invisible at the reported precision. Shown for transparency, not because it
moves the verdict — the gap is already negative before any cost is charged.

## The FX-drag regression — each leg's monthly return vs UUP (dollar-strength proxy)

| leg | β (vs UUP) | Newey-West *t* | correlation |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **Local** | **−1.050** | **−13.30** | −0.700 |
| EMB | −0.693 | −5.22 | −0.497 |
| AGG | −0.259 | −2.93 | −0.379 |
| **isolated: (Local − EMB) vs UUP** | **−0.358** | **−3.93** | −0.412 |

All three legs carry a negative dollar beta — a stronger US dollar is generically bad for EM
credit and even US aggregate bonds (a shared macro/duration channel, not FX alone). What
isolates the *incremental* currency channel is the last row: the Local-minus-EMB spread itself
is regressed on the dollar, and the relationship survives strongly (β = −0.358, Newey-West
*t* = −3.93) — every point the dollar index gains costs the local-vs-USD spread roughly 36 bps,
on top of whatever EMB itself already loses.

## Named crisis windows — cumulative return inside each episode

| window | n (mo) | Local | EMB | AGG | dollar (UUP) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2013 taper tantrum (May–Dec) | 8 | **−8.59%** | −7.73% | −2.98% | −3.06% |
| 2015 EM-FX selloff (Aug–Dec) | 5 | **−5.54%** | −1.03% | −0.04% | +0.87% |
| 2022 strong dollar (Jan–Oct) | 10 | **−19.06%** | −25.06% | −15.48% | +17.17% |

Mixed at the episode level: in 2013 and especially 2015, local debt fell well past EMB while the
dollar barely moved or ticked up slightly — the currency leg amplified the drawdown exactly as
the FX-drag story predicts. **2022 breaks the pattern** — despite the dollar's biggest surge of
the sample (+17.2%), Local actually *outperformed* EMB (−19.1% vs −25.1%): 2022 was primarily a
global-duration shock (the fastest Fed hiking cycle since the 1980s), and EMB's longer duration
and pure USD-credit exposure took the bigger hit that year. Episode-level results are not
uniform; the full-sample regression above is the more reliable read.

## Max drawdown (peak-to-trough, full sample)

| leg | max drawdown | date |
|---|--:|---|
| Local | **−27.47%** | 2022-10-31 |
| EMB | −26.74% | 2022-10-31 |
| AGG | −17.13% | 2022-10-31 |

All three bottomed on the same date — the 2022 duration shock, not an idiosyncratic EM-FX
event, drove the worst drawdown of the sample for every leg.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (local, usd) monthly-return world with an independent "extra yield"
(`yield_pickup`) knob and an independent dollar-tied "drag" knob; no network.

| world | mean gap (ann) | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| null (`yield_pickup=0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.22** (sd 0.86), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** | |
| planted `yield_pickup=+2.5 bps/mo` (+3.0%/yr), no drag (seed 662) | **+2.47%** | **+2.36** |
| illustrative: same pickup + full-strength dollar drag matched to UUP's own secular drift (seed 662) | −1.42% | −0.63 |

The null fires in 1/20 seeds — consistent with the ~5% nominal false-positive rate of a
two-sided *t*-test at the |t| ≥ 1.96 threshold, not a bias in the harness. A genuine, undragged
extra-yield world is recovered cleanly (*t* = +2.36); adding a dollar-tied drag calibrated to
the real UUP tape's own secular drift erases it. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp; the third row is a narrative illustration, not a
certification requirement.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed benefit — local-currency EM debt paying a better
  risk-compensated carry than USD EM debt — does not appear on the tape. If anything, the tape
  shows the **opposite**, robustly: Local underperformed EMB by **−2.96%/yr** on an
  excess-of-cash basis, clearing **|t| ≥ 2** at every Newey-West lag choice (3/6/12 months:
  −2.02 / −2.16 / −2.17), with a block-bootstrap 95% CI **entirely below zero** and a 41.5% hit
  rate (Wilson excludes 50%). A significant reversal of the claim reads `NONE`, not `REAL` —
  the desk's convention when a tested payoff comes back statistically real but the wrong sign
  (see [339-convertible-bonds](../339-convertible-bonds/)).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Local's own excess-of-cash Sharpe over 14.5 years is **−0.023** —
  worse than EMB's +0.296 and AGG's +0.138 — for **−27.5%** max drawdown and a highly
  significant, uncompensated dollar beta (−1.05, *t* = −13.3). There is no residual edge here to
  protect from costs; the point estimate is already negative before any cost is charged.
- **"Is the extra yield eaten by currency depreciation?" — CONFIRMED.** The isolated
  Local-minus-EMB spread regressed on the dollar clears the bar decisively (β = −0.358,
  Newey-West *t* = −3.93): every point of dollar strength costs the local-vs-USD spread ~36 bps
  beyond what EMB itself already loses. Caveat named: the mechanism is not uniform
  episode-by-episode — 2022's global duration shock hit EMB harder than Local despite the
  dollar's biggest rally of the sample — but the full-sample regression, the more reliable
  read, is unambiguous.
